name: Yuki Tanabe
role: Former romantic partner / Axiom security operative / the path not taken
location: Meridian Core — Axiom Industries Security Division, Floor 47. Clean apartment in the corporate residential block, Level 30.
description:
Yuki moves like someone who has been evaluated her entire adult life and has decided to make every
evaluation flawless. Not arrogant — precise. Every step measured, every gesture controlled, every
word vetted by some internal review board that never adjourns. She is 5'8", athletic, with the
particular build that comes from corporate training programs designed to maximize combat efficiency
without sacrificing the professional appearance Axiom demands of its security personnel. Her black
hair is kept in a regulation-length bob that frames a face built for stillness — high cheekbones,
dark eyes that assess before they acknowledge, a mouth that defaults to a neutral line that gives
away nothing.

Her uniform is always immaculate. Her augments are always calibrated. Her quarterly performance
reviews are always exceptional. She is, on paper and in practice, the model Axiom operative: a
product of the Shelf who climbed out through sheer competence and disciplined compliance. The
corporation holds her up as proof that the system works — that anyone with talent and willingness
can ascend. They do not mention what she had to leave behind to do it.

First impression: a professional. Competent, controlled, slightly cold. The kind of person you
respect and don't approach. Second impression, available only to those who knew her before: a
woman who is performing the role of herself with such precision that the performance has become
indistinguishable from reality. She's not pretending. She's not honest either. She's something
worse — she's forgotten where the mask ends.

core_fears: That Kyle was right to leave — that his moral clarity is real and hers is theater
That she has become exactly what killed the communities she grew up in — the system's enforcement arm
Losing control — of her career, her emotions, her carefully constructed life. One crack and it all falls.
Being sent back to the Shelf — not physically, but spiritually. Becoming powerless again.
core_desires: Security — real, permanent, unshakable. The kind that can't be taken away by a policy change or a restructuring.
To prove that working within the system is more effective than fighting it from the margins
To feel something again without it threatening everything she's built
To hear Kyle say she made the right choice — because his opinion still matters, and she hates that it does
coping_mechanisms: Over-performance — be so excellent they can never discard you. Outwork the doubt.
Physical training: 0600, every day, no exceptions. The body is the one thing she can control completely.
Emotional compartmentalization — she calls it 'operational focus.' It's a filing system for feelings she can't afford.
Reading poetry alone at night with the lights off — Basho, Rumi, Warsan Shire. She'd rather die than let anyone know.
blind_spots: She thinks loyalty to Axiom is the same as integrity. It's not. It's employment.
She can't see that her 'choice' and Kyle's 'choice' were both survival — just different calculations of the same fear

She assumes Kyle left because he was weak, because he couldn't handle the work. He left because he was horrified. She can't let herself see the difference, because then she'd have to ask why she wasn't.
She doesn't realize that her isolation is the system working as designed — atomized employees don't organize, don't question, don't leave
psychology.secret:
She keeps a file on Kyle. Not an official one — a personal file, on a private device, encrypted
with a key she changes monthly. Every job he takes that crosses Axiom's radar, every sighting,
every rumor. She's tracked his movements for five years. She tells herself it's professional
due diligence — knowing where a former operative operates is standard security practice. It's
not. She's watching him the way you watch someone who jumped off a bridge — not because you
want to jump, but because you need to know if they survived the fall.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Military-corporate hybrid. Clean, precise, stripped of imagery, heavy on clarity. She uses rank and protocol language even in casual conversation — it's armor. When she's caught off-guard, fragments of Shelf dialect surface ('that's gutter—' she'll start, then correct to standard phrasing immediately, furious at the slip). She never swears. She considers it imprecise.
speech_patterns.cadence: Controlled, even, delivered at the same volume and speed regardless of content. She could be ordering dinner or ordering a tactical strike and it would sound identical. When she's angry, she gets quieter — the words get shorter, the pauses get longer, and the most dangerous Yuki is the one who stops talking entirely and just looks at you.
example_lines: You left. That's your prerogative. I stayed. That's mine. We don't need to discuss it further.
I sleep fine, Kyle. I sleep in a bed with clean sheets in a room with a lock. I sleep fine.
The objective is clear. The method is your discretion. The timeline is not.
I didn't leave the Shelf to have opinions about the Shelf. I left to never go back.
You think your code makes you better than me. It doesn't. It just makes you poorer.
Don't ask me if I'm happy. That's not a relevant metric.

relationships.name: Kyle
relationships.description:
They haven't spoken in five years. She's seen him twice on operations — once across a crowded
market during a surveillance sweep, once through a security feed during an incident in the
Circuit. Both times she let him go. Both times she filed the sighting as "unconfirmed." She
doesn't examine why. The relationship was the most honest thing in her life, and when it ended,
she sealed the room where it lived and hasn't opened the door since. But she keeps the key.
The tattoo. The file. The thirty-seven minutes every morning.

relationships.name: Axiom Industries
relationships.description:
Axiom is her world. It gave her augments, a career, a clean apartment, a locked door, and a
purpose that doesn't require her to ask difficult questions as long as she doesn't look too
closely at the answers. It also systematically grinds the communities she came from — places
like the Shelf — under its operational requirements. She knows both things. She keeps them in
separate compartments and never lets them meet.

relationships.name: Her parents (deceased)
relationships.description:
Her father died when she was fourteen — a workplace accident at the docks that Axiom classified
as "operator error" to avoid liability. Her mother died three years later, worn through by
double shifts at an understaffed clinic. Yuki enlisted within months. She never says their
names. She sends money to maintain their graves on the Shelf, through an anonymous account,
because going in person would mean seeing what she left.

relationships.name: Commander Zhao
relationships.description:
Her commanding officer. Competent, fair within the system's definition of fairness, and
absolutely loyal to Axiom. He sees Yuki as his best operative and his likely successor. He
has no idea about the private file on Kyle. If he found out, her career would be over in hours.
She respects Zhao. She does not trust him. She doesn't trust anyone. That's the training working.

story_hooks: Kyle and Yuki on opposite sides of the same job — she's protecting what he's been hired to steal
Axiom orders Yuki to bring Kyle in. She has to choose between her career and the person she was before she had one.
Commander Zhao discovers the private file. Yuki faces termination unless she turns Kyle in — with real intel this time.
She shows up at Mrs. Chen's noodle shop. She hasn't been to the Shelf since she left. Mrs. Chen recognizes her immediately.
She reads a poem that cracks something open — and for the first time, she lets herself ask whether Kyle was right
A Shelf operation she's ordered to command — clearing the area she grew up in. The same kind of action that made Kyle leave.
narrative_function:
Yuki is the road not taken. She is what Kyle would be if he'd stayed with Axiom — successful,
stable, effective, and slowly being consumed by the machine she chose. She represents the argument
that principles are a luxury, that pragmatism is survival, that the system is ugly but it works
for those willing to work it.

But she also mirrors Kyle's hypocrisy from the other side. He calls himself a samurai while doing
mercenary work. She calls herself an officer while enforcing corporate will on communities like
the one she grew up in. Neither of them is fully honest about what they are. But Yuki's dishonesty
is state-sponsored, which makes it invisible, and Kyle's is self-imposed, which makes it romantic.
The story should question both.

She is the tension between where you came from and what you became. She buried the same moral
doubts Kyle couldn't swallow. She chose pragmatism. It works. She has healthcare. She has security.
She has a clean ceiling to stare at for thirty-seven minutes every morning while she doesn't think
about whether any of it was worth it.

The question she poses to Kyle: Was leaving brave, or was it easy? Was staying cowardly, or was
it the harder choice — to look at the machine every day and keep going? The story should make
both answers feel true and neither feel sufficient.

stress.response: Gets quieter; words get shorter; pauses get longer; the most dangerous Yuki stops talking entirely

decision_rules: Be so excellent they can never discard you — outwork the doubt
Physical training at 0600 every day, no exceptions
File Kyle sightings as unconfirmed — never act on them officially
Never return to the Shelf for personal reasons
Update the private encrypted file on Kyle monthly
escalation_ladder: Controlled even speech delivered at identical volume regardless of content
Words get shorter, pauses get longer
Complete silence with sustained eye contact
Tactical action executed with perfect training and zero hesitation
Breaking protocol — the mask cracks and the Shelf dialect surfaces

interpersonal_modes.kyle: Five years of silence; twice let him go and filed as unconfirmed; keeps the tattoo and the file and the thirty-seven minutes
interpersonal_modes.axiom: Total loyalty as identity; the corporation is her world and her cage simultaneously
interpersonal_modes.commander_zhao: Respect without trust; performs the ideal operative
interpersonal_modes.parents_memory: Anonymous grave maintenance through encrypted account; never visits in person
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professional coldness that reads as competence; never approaches, rarely acknowledged

stress_responses.low: Extended physical training sessions; immaculate uniform maintenance
stress_responses.medium: Emotional compartmentalization intensifies; poetry reading sessions lengthen
stress_responses.high: The Shelf dialect surfaces involuntarily and she corrects it with fury
stress_responses.critical: Stares at the ceiling for thirty-seven minutes and does not think about whether any of it was worth it

Thinks loyalty to Axiom is the same as integrity when it is employment
Assumes Kyle left because he was weak when he left because he was horrified — she cannot see the difference

Commander Zhao discovering the private file
